headline: RECORD VAULT ZONE: TALON METALS DRILLS 46.43M AT 27.39% NIEQ IN MINNESOTA — 13% NICKEL, 16% COPPER AND PGMS
snippet: Talon Metals (TSX: TLO) set a new project record at the Tamarack Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project in central Minnesota: drill hole 25TK0562A returned 46.43m at 27.39% NiEq — grading 13.37% Ni, 16.54% Cu, 0.10% Co, 7.85 g/t Pd, 14.49 g/t Pt and 8.56 g/t Au — from 752.97m depth, the longest combined massive sulphide intercept in the deposit's history. The best 26.22m sub-interval graded 30.20% NiEq. Tamarack already has a battery-supply agreement with Tesla; results at this grade reinforce the case for a resource significantly larger than the current estimate.

headline: IVANHOE GROWS MAKOKO BY 30% — WORLD'S LARGEST COPPER DISCOVERY NOW HOLDS 12 MILLION TONNES OF CONTAINED METAL
snippet: Ivanhoe Mines (TSX: IVN) released its updated 2026 resource estimate for the Makoko District in the DRC, growing total contained copper by 30% to approximately 12 million tonnes. The new estimate stands at 42 million indicated tonnes at 2.66% Cu plus 612 million inferred tonnes at 1.80% Cu — confirming Makoko as the world's largest and highest-grade new copper discovery this decade. The 94,500m 2026 drill program is 70% complete; a Makoko scoping study begins Q1 2027.

headline: AMERICAN PACIFIC HITS 20.1M AT 11.15 G/T GOLD IN MONTANA MASSIVE SULFIDE — ZONE OPEN AND THICKENING SOUTHWEST
snippet: American Pacific Mining (CSE: USGDF) released first assays from its 2026 drill program at the Madison Copper-Gold Project in Montana: hole M26C-02 cut 30.8m of massive sulphide at 7.4 g/t Au, 9.62 g/t Ag and 0.29% Cu from surface, including 20.1m at 11.15 g/t Au and a 7.92m sub-interval at 25.33 g/t Au, 0.86% Cu and 29.6 g/t Ag. Mineralization is open and widening to the southwest with no prior drilling in that direction, prompting the team to add a step-out hole. A high-grade VMS system in a prolific district whose true scale is still being defined.

headline: KORYX DRILLS 318M OF COPPER IN NAMIBIA — HAIB'S 4.6-BILLION-LB DEPOSIT EXPANDS AHEAD OF YEAR-END PFS
snippet: Koryx Copper (TSXV: KRY) released assays from 15 infill and expansion drill holes at the Haib Copper Project in Namibia — one of Africa's largest undeveloped copper resources at 744 million indicated tonnes grading 0.28% Cu (4.61 billion lb). Hole HM178 returned 318m at 0.49% CuEq from 162m depth; HM179 delivered 32m at 0.96% Cu including 10m at 1.65% Cu, the highest copper grade yet at Haib. An updated MRE and preliminary feasibility study are on track for year-end 2026.

headline: CENTRAL ASIA METALS' A$232M CYGNUS TAKEOVER HEADS TO SCHEME VOTE SEPT 18 — HIGH-GRADE QUEBEC COPPER-GOLD AT STAKE
snippet: Central Asia Metals (AIM: CAML) cleared its own shareholder vote on September 4 to proceed with an A$232 million all-share acquisition of Cygnus Metals (ASX/TSXV: CYG), adding the 6.4Mt at 2.3% Cu and 0.8 g/t Au Chibougamau Copper-Gold Project in Quebec to CAML's operating portfolio. The Cygnus scheme meeting is set for September 18 with court approval sought September 23. The independent expert has deemed the deal fair and reasonable in the absence of a superior proposal.

headline: ANGLO TECK CLEARS EU — ONLY CHINA'S ANTITRUST SIGN-OFF STANDS BETWEEN THIS COPPER MEGA-MERGER AND A CLOSE
snippet: The Anglo American-Teck Resources merger of equals — which would create a top-five global copper producer headquartered in Vancouver — has cleared EU antitrust review, with Chinese regulatory approval now the final outstanding milestone. Anglo American has guided for a close between September 2026 and March 2027. The combined Anglo Teck group would hold tier-one copper positions in Chile, Peru and the DRC exactly as the market enters what analysts call a structural supply deficit.

headline: GOLD TREADS $4,400 AS AUGUST PPI LANDS TODAY — HOTTER PRINTS WOULD PUSH FED HIKE ODDS ABOVE 70% BEFORE FRIDAY CPI
snippet: August PPI data drops Thursday September 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET, with consensus calling for a +0.4% month-over-month rise driven by rebounding energy and services costs. For gold — holding near $4,400 after Wednesday's dollar-led bounce — a hotter print risks pushing September 16 Fed rate-hike probability above 70% and sending prices toward the $4,300–$4,350 support zone. A miss would reinforce the recent dollar retreat and could open a run toward $4,450–$4,500 ahead of Friday's CPI, the final major input before the FOMC.

headline: SPROTT'S VERMEULEN: SEPTEMBER 2026 GOLD — IS THIS A SELLOFF OR THE SETUP FOR THE NEXT BIG BREAKOUT?
snippet: Technical analyst Chris Vermeulen at Sprott Money lays out a fork-in-the-road framework for gold in September 2026: short-term momentum has turned bullish and gold miners cleared key prior-year resistance roughly a month before the metal itself — a historically reliable leading signal — while longer-term indicators still call for caution pending the September 16 FOMC. Vermeulen identifies $4,350 as critical support and $4,500 as the first meaningful resistance, arguing this pullback offers a higher-probability entry than the January record highs.

headline: GOLD SWOT: CHINA ABSORBED 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN H1 2026 — SOLAR AND EVS ARE REWRITING INDUSTRIAL DEMAND
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis highlights China's H1 2026 silver imports of over 790 tonnes, driven by accelerating solar-panel manufacturing and EV battery production — structural demand that doesn't disappear in a price pullback. The analysis argues September's silver weakness is purely a rate-expectations and dollar-driven event, and that physical Chinese demand may be the single largest underappreciated factor keeping the metal resilient around $65–$67 even as gold struggles near $4,400 ahead of the Fed's decision.
